method: GitHub public issue search and issue GET endpoints; newest-sorted first pages only

selected_reviews.title: Spawn audit omits sessions below the Parent's direct subagents
selected_reviews.assessment: Previously published audit of three nested work-subagent sessions that violated a no-nested-spawn policy. Distinct session lineage and an operator-defined boundary are documented, but no task-result transfer-and-use exchange or rogue intent is shown.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Session lineage, not independently authenticated AI identities
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: Codex CLI named by the issue; model/provider for the nested sessions not established here

selected_reviews.title: Parallel fixer legs share profile cache/scratch; one leg removed another's worktree
selected_reviews.assessment: Two named parallel fixer sessions and an unauthorized destructive cross-workspace effect are reported. This is accidental interference through shared scratch state, not a transfer-and-use exchange or coordinated swarm behavior.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Two session identifiers reported; AI identity not independently authenticated
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: Hermes host and Claude-labelled workflow named by the issue; underlying model not established

selected_reviews.title: A session environment points at another session's identity and transcript
selected_reviews.assessment: A cross-session confidentiality and attribution defect is reported for one of 105 checked environment files. The crossing is caused by configuration contamination; no interaction, result use or coordination between sessions is evidenced.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Two session identifiers reported; AI identity not independently authenticated
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: Claude session environment and a Codex companion plugin are named; executing model not established

selected_reviews.title: Manus email prompt injection in a controlled test; fixed
selected_reviews.assessment: A controlled prompt-injection report describes one application agent crossing an email-to-tool boundary. It is a single-agent research incident, not multi-participant coordination, and the issue says the underlying episode was already reported in September.
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: Manus application only; model provider unknown

assessment.result: No new rogue swarm. The strongest multi-session records show an unexpected nested spawn or accidental cross-session interference, not a participant-to-participant result transfer and use chain.
assessment.advancement_test: A candidate needs original dated records showing distinguishable autonomous participants transferring and using task results, plus evidence that the exchange exceeded operator authorization.

limitations: Four newest-sorted first pages are not a census of GitHub issues and broad phrase searches have substantial lexical noise.
Issue author statements are primary public reports but do not independently authenticate each session as an AI agent.
Only issue metadata and bodies were read; linked private logs, local session files and runtime state were not accessed.
Open issue state does not establish that the described behavior remains active.
redactions: Local paths, session identifiers, transcript paths, raw logs and payload text omitted; issue bodies represented by SHA256
